column1: # The test manifest: the single source of truth for what exists and how to run it.
# Both the Makefile and run_tier.py read this file. The Makefile uses columns
# 1-3 to generate a build rule per target; the runner uses all six. Two lints
# run as part of `make check`: a *_check.cpp with no row here fails, and a row
# with no source file fails. That is what keeps targets from going unbuilt --
# before this file, `make all` built 2 of 23 and the other 21 rotted quietly
# (klut_identify_check had stopped compiling; link_alex_probe was exiting 1).
#   target      binary name (and, unless `source` says otherwise, <target>.cpp)
#   kind        test  -- runs with no arguments, exit 0 = pass. Runs in the tiers.
#               tool  -- needs arguments or input to do anything. Built, never run.
#               bench -- measures rather than asserts. Built, never run.
#   needs       link shape; picks FLAGS_/LIBS_/DEPS_ in the Makefile:
#   source      source file, if it is not <target>.cpp
#   light-args  argv for the light tier (must still do real work -- see §7)
#   heavy-args  argv for the heavy tier
#   work        a regex that the run's stdout MUST match, in BOTH tiers.
#               This is the guard against a reduced test quietly becoming a
#               no-op. The light tier shrinks --trials, --target and
#               --up-to-crossing; shrink one too far and the test still exits 0
#               having examined nothing, which is worse than a failure because
#               it reads as coverage. So the pattern must match a count of work
#               -- and must not match when that count is zero. A "0 failures"
#               line is exactly the wrong thing to match: it is most true when
# Keep the columns aligned with tabs only; the parsers split on '\t'.
